subject.title: [Feature]: Add runtime testing for skill workshop proposals before apply

question: Should Skill Workshop pre-apply runtime validation start as load/discovery/schema smoke checks only, or should the first core implementation also support sandboxed representative invocation of proposed skills?
rationale: Executing or simulating pending skill behavior before apply changes the approval and side-effect boundary, and the repository cannot infer the acceptable sandbox/tool-policy contract from existing code.

options.title: Start with smoke-test validation
options.body: Add a shared validation result for proposal loadability, registry discovery, and tool schema visibility, while marking invocation as skipped until a safe test-case contract exists.

options.title: Define sandboxed invocation now
options.body: Require a fuller design for representative inputs, allowed tools, network/filesystem isolation, side-effect assertions, and override semantics before implementation begins.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle-contract work
options.body: Keep this as a subtask of the broader Skill Workshop lifecycle-contract issue and implement runtime testing only after that contract has an owner-approved shape.

recommendation.title: Start with smoke-test validation
recommendation.body: Add a shared validation result for proposal loadability, registry discovery, and tool schema visibility, while marking invocation as skipped until a safe test-case contract exists.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest path history on the Skill Workshop service, CLI, Gateway, docs, and tool actions that would need one shared validation contract.
